![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

To prevent rendering issues or property-access crashes when rendering items in the `saved` array, we should defensively clean and filter the array elements to ensure they are valid, non-empty strings.

```suggestion
    saved: safeArray(source.saved).map((v) => cleanString(v)).filter(Boolean),
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

We can optimize this by calling `safeArray` only once, and defensively map and filter the `statusOptions` array to ensure it contains only valid, non-empty strings before falling back to `fallbackStatusOptions`.

```suggestion
export function normalizeDetailTask(task) {
  const source = isPlainObject(task) ? task : {};
  const statusOptions = safeArray(source.statusOptions).map((v) => cleanString(v)).filter(Boolean);

  return {
    ...source,
    id: cleanString(source.id ?? source.reviewTaskId, 'review-task-unset'),
    evidence: source.evidence ?? source.evidenceState ?? 'unverified',
    statusOptions: statusOptions.length ? statusOptions : [...fallbackStatusOptions],
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Instead of performing inline lookups and fallback logic within the component, prefer using a dedicated normalization helper function to defensively handle nullish or undefined lookup results (by providing default structures and filtering unresolved related lookups) over inline fallback objects within components.

```suggestion
        const task = getNormalizedLinkedTask(repairGroup, linkedReviewTaskById);
        const reviewTaskId = task.id;
```
